business.about: HDFC Bank Limited (also known as HDFC) is an Indian banking and financial services company headquartered in Mumbai. It is India's largest private sector bank by assets and the world's tenth-largest bank by market capitalization as of May 2024. As of April 2024, HDFC Bank has a market capitalization of $145 billion, making it the third-largest company on the Indian stock exchanges. [1]

promises.opening: welcome to HDFC Bank Limited Q2 FY27 Earnings Conference Call on the financial results presented by the management of HDFC Bank. As a reminder, all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode, and there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Should you need assistance during this conference call, please signal an operator by pressing star, then zero on your touch-tone phone. Please note that this conference is being recorded. I now hand the conference over to Mr. Srinivasan Vaidyanathan, Chief Financial Officer, HDFC Bank. Thank you, and over to you, Mr. Vaidyanathan. Srinivasan Vaidyanathan: Okay. Thank you, Neerav. Good evening, and a warm welcome to all the participants. Today, we have with us Sashi, Anup and Kaizad. Without much ado, we'll get the meeting started. With Sashi, for your opening remarks first, please. Sashidhar Jagdishan: Thank you, Srini, and thank you, everyone. Let me start with the economic environment. The GDP growth in Q2 FY27 has been better than anticipated and high performance indicators such as industrial production, strong e-way bill, cargo activity, credit growth reflects sustained momentum. Retail consumption growth has also been robust with passenger vehicles, 2-wheeler sales all growing upwards of 30-plus percentage. Even consumer durables grew at about 11% year-on-year. This augurs very well for the economy, especially with the festive season underway. The broader policy environment has been supportive of economic activity. Alongside this, measures in the form of credit guarantee support to MSMEs have also been effective. RBI's proactive response through measures like the special FCNR (B) swap window generated record inflows, about $133 billion and helped stabilize the currency. With that background, let's take a quick look at how the business has been shaping up. We continue to strengthen our liabilities franchise, and it has been delivering with great vigor. Deposits increased 18.8% year-on-year on a reported basis, including a 4 percentage point lift from special FCNR (B) window. As you will see in our published deck, CASA grew at about 10.8% on an overall basis. And within this, retail CASA growth was about 11.2% year-on-year compared to 9% a year ago, reflecting improving momentum. We added about 1.7 million liability relationships in the second quarter, which is 25% higher than Q1 and 33% higher than the fourth quarter of last year. Building on these new acquired relationships and deepening our existing relationships will enable the liabilities engine to step up further in the coming days even as we keep adding newer relationships at a rapid pace. The asset side of the balance sheet also continued to get stronger. Total AUM grew 15.3% year- on-year, including a 1.9% impact of FCNR (B) leverage, with SME and retail assets leading the charge. The pace of retail disbursements is accelerating and has crossed Rs 90,000 crores during Q2 FY27 as against Rs 76,000 crores in Q1 of this year. Growth has been balanced across all lines, whether it's personal loans, the wheels business, gold and agri and other MSME business as well. This is also reflected in the rising growth trend in EOP HDFC Bank Limited October 17, 2026 Page 3 of 16 loan book, especially for retail assets ex agri, September'26 annual growth is about 11.2% compared to 9.1% as of June'26 and 7.4% as of March'26. New credit card issuances at 1.4 million have grown by nearly 19% quarter-on-quarter, indicating the expansion of the growth runway. On the MSME and mid-market business, growth momentum is also improving rapidly. September'26 EOP loan growth has grown 23.5% year-on-year compared to 17% to 18% year-on-year growth levels seen in the last few quarters. Of course, this quarter, we have the ECLGS 5.0 scheme that also created significant opportunities we successfully leveraged.
